newsitem.title: UK: Doctors announce quick, new treatment for ulcers.
newsitem.headline: Doctors announce quick, new treatment for ulcers.

text.p: Scottish scientists said on Thursday that they have found a new method to cure chronic stomach ulcers in a week.

"Up until now, ulcer patients have had to take repeated courses of acid inhibitory drugs to keep their ulcers disease under control," Professor Kenneth McColl of Glasgow University told Reuters. "Their condition can now be cured with a single one-week course of antibiotics."
McColl, an expert in the treatment of stomach ulcers, launched new guidelines for family doctors to ensure that every ulcer patient received the benefit of the new treatment.

Ulcers cause recurrent stomach pain and frequently complications from bleeding or perforation of the stomach lining occur. Patients usually develop ulcers between the ages of 20 and 50, with smokers being the most common victims.

Scottish scientists have spent 10 years searching for the best way to treat gastric and duodenal ulcers. Their discovery that a bacterium carried by around half the world's population causes an infection that ulcerates the stomach lining pointed the way to a cure.

The bacterium helicobacter pylori, discovered 10 years ago by Australian doctor Barry Marshall, can be eradicated by a week-long course of three widely available antibiotics which costs about 30 pounds ($47).
"This is one of the few permanent cures we have for a chronic illness," McColl said.
But he cautioned that the treatment did not offer a cure for all stomach ailments.
It provided a cure in more than 95 percent of ulcer cases but three in every four suspected ulcer patients were found to have other illnesses, he said.

Researchers pointed out that the same bacterium was present in many cases of stomach or colon cancer and the medication was being tested to see if it could be used to treat these diseases. ($1=.6388 Pound)
